title: Design System: Axis Specimen
scope: tools/listening_game.html, future surfaces in the same world, and (since 14 Nov, agreed by Student B and Developer B) Developer B's React app in web/ (web/src/styles.css). The app keeps its NASA image in the main column, not the rail.

numeral.purpose: Giant patch numbers 1 and 2; weight 500 at rest, 200 to 800 from alignment on reveal; Paper stroke halo; overlaps the image's lower edge by 0.32em.

value.purpose: Alignment number under each numeral; weight set by alignment; 1.9rem under 640px.

headline.purpose: The page question in the rail.

status.purpose: Live status sentence at the top of main, aria-live polite, max 46ch.

readout.purpose: Mono tabular readouts: slider outputs, note and wght lines, table numbers.

motion.name: snap
motion.purpose: Every state change, including numeral font-weight on reveal. No easing. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Rail and main stack: top rail, main, bottom rail; 16px gutter.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Patch gap 14px; readouts stack; Value drops to 1.9rem.

narrative.overview:
The page is a type specimen for one measurement. Every alignment number is set in a variable sans whose weight is the value itself: a swirly patch's numeral reads as a hairline, a lined-up one as a slab. The page around those numerals stays still and quiet: cool paper, near-black ink, hairline rules, square 4px corners. One signal orange marks what is live or chosen. The NASA image is the only full-spectrum colour on screen, and the system never competes with it.

Density is a working instrument, not a quiz app. A fixed 400px left rail holds the map, playback, settings and score. The main column holds the status sentence, two equal patch columns and one shared plot. State changes snap in two 90ms steps with no easing, like an acetate overlay being swapped.
keyCharacteristics: Type weight carries data: variable `wght` 200 to 800 maps an alignment of 0 to 1.
One accent (signal orange) for selection, focus, the live state and the high pulse.
Flat surfaces, 1px hairline rules, 4px corners, no shadows.
Mono readouts with tabular figures beside every control and value.
Keyboard first: every action shows its key in a key cap.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange is the only accent. It means "chosen, live or focused" and nothing else. No second hue is introduced for right/wrong; the answer is shown in Ink.

rules.name: The Image Owns Colour Rule
rules.body: The NASA visualization is the only full-spectrum colour. Chrome stays in paper, ink and rule greys so the data image is never repainted or competed with.

rules.name: The Weight Is the Value Rule
rules.body: Alignment numbers and patch numerals take `font-weight` from the measured alignment (200 at the swirly end, 800 at the lined-up end). Before the answer they sit at a neutral 500 so the page gives nothing away. Never use weight for emphasis on these elements.

rules.name: The Mono Readout Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes while you watch (slider outputs, alignment note and weight lines, scores) is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is a 1px Rule Grey line, not a card, not a shadow, not a tinted panel.

dos: **Do** drive the weight of every alignment numeral from the value (200 to 800), and hold it at 500 until the answer is shown.
**Do** reserve Signal Orange for the chosen, live or focused thing, with Ink text on it.
**Do** animate state changes as a two-step 90ms snap (`steps(2, jump-end)`), and remove transitions under reduced motion.
**Do** set live numbers in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** show each action's keyboard key in a key cap inside its button.
**Do** keep the NASA credit directly under the image it credits.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent or green/red right/wrong colours; the answer is shown with Ink.
**Don't** use shadows, cards or tinted panels; separate sections with 1px Rule Grey lines.
**Don't** tint, recolour or overlay colour on the NASA imagery beyond the black-and-white region boxes.
**Don't** use eased or springy motion; the world snaps.
